dct_description_sm: The built boundary identifies built-up urban areas across the Greater Golden Horseshoe. It is a fixed line that reflects what was built and on the ground when the Growth Plan came into effect in June 2006. The boundaries are an important implementation and monitoring tool for the Growth Plan for the Greater Golden Horseshoe. The built boundary will allow the province and others to measure intensification and redevelopment within the built-up area, and also allow us to monitor suburban development outside the built-up area. The built boundary was released in its final form on April 2, 2008, along with the methodology used to create it.In June 2019, TRCA staff manually updated the layer to incorporate recently built up areas (post-2006) based on most current available aerial photography, excepting Richmond Hill “Settlement Areas” on the ORM. (“Settlement Areas” is a land use designation in the ORM Conservation Plan.)  In 2020, the GGH boundary was updated according to Policy & Planning's suggestion.
dct_title_s: ECWP Whitebelt Boundary in Headwaters Subwatershed
